headline: Canada International Experience Canada (IEC) 2026: Working Holiday Guide
metaDescription: Canada's IEC 2026 guide: 36 partner countries, ages 18 to 35, Working Holiday, Young Professionals and Co-op categories, fees, funds and invitation draws.

sections.content:
International Experience Canada, run by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, lets young people from 36 partner countries live and work in Canada for up to 24 months. The program operates through bilateral Youth Mobility Agreements and is designed as a cultural exchange: participants fund their travels with short-term work while experiencing Canadian life.

The 2026 season opened on 19 December 2025, with approximately 61,189 spots available across all countries and categories. Invitations for the season began in the week of 19 January 2026 and continue in regular draw rounds until quotas fill. Because selection is a lottery, timing and eligibility matter more than applying first.
sections.title: What Is International Experience Canada?

sections.content:
IEC has three categories. Working Holiday is the most popular: it gives an open work permit, so you can work for almost any employer anywhere in Canada, with no job offer required. Permits last 12 months for most countries and up to 24 months for citizens of the UK, France, Ireland, Australia, Portugal and South Korea.

Young Professionals offers an employer-specific permit tied to a skilled job offer that advances your career, and self-employment is excluded. International Co-op is for students who need an internship or work placement in their field of study. Switzerland participates only in Young Professionals and Co-op, which require a job offer or internship before applying.
sections.title: The Three IEC Categories

sections.content:
Eligibility depends on your citizenship: you must hold a passport from one of the 36 participating countries, which include Australia, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Japan, New Zealand, Spain, South Korea, Taiwan and the United Kingdom. The United States, China, India, the Philippines, Brazil and Mexico do not have active IEC agreements, although US citizens can participate through a recognised organisation.

Most countries accept applicants aged 18 to 35, while Andorra, Belgium, Hong Kong, Iceland, Japan, the Netherlands and Sweden cap eligibility at 30. The age rule applies when you receive your Invitation to Apply, so you may turn 36 during your permit without losing it. You must also show at least 2,500 Canadian dollars on arrival, hold health insurance for your entire stay, and have a return ticket or funds to buy one.
sections.title: Who Is Eligible?

sections.content:
Applying starts on canada.ca with the Come to Canada questionnaire, which gives you a personal reference code. You then create an IRCC secure account, build your IEC profile and enter every pool you qualify for; the profile itself is free. When you receive an Invitation to Apply, you submit your full work permit application with supporting documents.

Fees for Working Holiday total 284.75 Canadian dollars, plus 85 dollars for biometrics where required. Some countries allow multiple participations: Australia, Austria, Finland, France and Ireland allow three, many countries allow two, and several allow only one. Check your country's specific rules before applying, since a profile from an earlier season does not carry over.
